The PR propagates TLS profile configuration through the operator. The canary controller now watches the cluster APIServer resource, reads its TLSSecurityProfile (falling back to Intermediate when missing), and passes a computed TLSProfileSpec into canary DaemonSet creation. DaemonSet templates add TLS_CIPHERS and TLS_MIN_VERSION env vars when a spec is provided. A new controller-level `TLSProfileSpecForSecurityProfile` and `copyTLSSpec` were added and reused by ingress logic. The healthcheck server reads TLS_CIPHERS and TLS_MIN_VERSION from environment variables. Tests were updated to exercise these changes.

**Actionable comments posted: 1**
🧹 Nitpick comments (2)
pkg/operator/controller/tls.go (1)
`12-24`: **Return defensive copies from the exported helper.** `TLSProfileSpecForSecurityProfile` currently returns pointers to shared/global structs. A caller mutation can leak side effects across reconciles.
Diff suggestion ```diff func TLSProfileSpecForSecurityProfile(profile *configv1.TLSSecurityProfile) *configv1.TLSProfileSpec { + copySpec := func(in *configv1.TLSProfileSpec) *configv1.TLSProfileSpec { + if in == nil { + return &configv1.TLSProfileSpec{} + } + out := *in + out.Ciphers = append([]string(nil), in.Ciphers...) + return &out + } + if profile != nil { if profile.Type == configv1.TLSProfileCustomType { if profile.Custom != nil { - return &profile.Custom.TLSProfileSpec + return copySpec(&profile.Custom.TLSProfileSpec) } - return &configv1.TLSProfileSpec{} + return &configv1.TLSProfileSpec{} } else if spec, ok := configv1.TLSProfiles[profile.Type]; ok { - return spec + return copySpec(spec) } } - return configv1.TLSProfiles[configv1.TLSProfileIntermediateType] + return copySpec(configv1.TLSProfiles[configv1.TLSProfileIntermediateType]) } ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@pkg/operator/controller/tls.go` around lines 12 - 24, TLSProfileSpecForSecurityProfile returns pointers to shared/global TLSProfileSpec instances (from configv1.TLSProfiles and profile.Custom.TLSProfileSpec), which allows callers to mutate shared state; change it to always return a newly allocated defensive copy: when profile.Custom != nil copy the value of profile.Custom.TLSProfileSpec into a new configv1.TLSProfileSpec and return its pointer, when returning a spec from configv1.TLSProfiles[profile.Type] copy that spec into a new configv1.TLSProfileSpec and return its pointer, and for the default case return a copy of configv1.TLSProfiles[configv1.TLSProfileIntermediateType]; ensure every return produces a distinct instance. ```
test/http/serve-healthcheck.go (1)
`47-48`: **Normalize cipher tokens before conversion.** At Line 47, values from `TLS_CIPHERS` are split but not trimmed. A value like `"CIPHER1, CIPHER2"` can silently drop valid suites due to leading spaces.
Diff suggestion ```diff - openSSLNames := strings.Split(cipherEnv, ",") + raw := strings.Split(cipherEnv, ",") + openSSLNames := make([]string, 0, len(raw)) + for _, name := range raw { + if trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(name); trimmed != "" { + openSSLNames = append(openSSLNames, trimmed) + } + } ianaNames := crypto.OpenSSLToIANACipherSuites(openSSLNames) ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@test/http/serve-healthcheck.go` around lines 47 - 48, Split TLS_CIPHERS into tokens, then normalize each token by trimming whitespace and dropping empty strings before passing to crypto.OpenSSLToIANACipherSuites; specifically, transform cipherEnv into a slice where openSSLNames are produced by splitting cipherEnv, mapping strings.TrimSpace over each token (and filtering out ""), then call crypto.OpenSSLToIANACipherSuites(openSSLNames) so leading/trailing spaces don't cause valid suites to be lost. ```
🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. Inline comments: In `@pkg/operator/controller/canary/controller.go`: - Around line 220-224: The code currently swallows all errors from r.client.Get(types.NamespacedName{Name: "cluster"}, apiConfig) and always falls back to intermediate TLS, which hides real API/auth errors; update the handling so that after calling r.client.Get(...) you check the error type: if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) then keep the existing fallback to operatorcontroller.TLSProfileSpecForSecurityProfile, but for any other error return or propagate the error (or requeue) and log it clearly (include err) instead of treating it as a benign case; make changes around the r.client.Get call and the apiConfig/tlsProfileSpec assignment to implement this conditional error handling. --- Nitpick comments: In `@pkg/operator/controller/tls.go`: - Around line 12-24: TLSProfileSpecForSecurityProfile returns pointers to shared/global TLSProfileSpec instances (from configv1.TLSProfiles and profile.Custom.TLSProfileSpec), which allows callers to mutate shared state; change it to always return a newly allocated defensive copy: when profile.Custom != nil copy the value of profile.Custom.TLSProfileSpec into a new configv1.TLSProfileSpec and return its pointer, when returning a spec from configv1.TLSProfiles[profile.Type] copy that spec into a new configv1.TLSProfileSpec and return its pointer, and for the default case return a copy of configv1.TLSProfiles[configv1.TLSProfileIntermediateType]; ensure every return produces a distinct instance. In `@test/http/serve-healthcheck.go`: - Around line 47-48: Split TLS_CIPHERS into tokens, then normalize each token by trimming whitespace and dropping empty strings before passing to crypto.OpenSSLToIANACipherSuites; specifically, transform cipherEnv into a slice where openSSLNames are produced by splitting cipherEnv, mapping strings.TrimSpace over each token (and filtering out ""), then call crypto.OpenSSLToIANACipherSuites(openSSLNames) so leading/trailing spaces don't cause valid suites to be lost. ```
